Discover the Best Dresses for Every November Occasion

📅 Dec 02, 2022  |  Category: Entertainment  |  Read Source →

All products featured on Vogue are independently selected by our editors. However, we may earn affiliate revenue on this article and commission when you buy something.

No matter the occasion or season, there are always plenty of opportunities to wear a dress and, of course, an overwhelming number of options from which to pick. We’ve put together an edit of the best dresses of the month; check back every two weeks for a new selection of styles, handpicked by Vogue.

There’s no better time than mid-November to embrace a little holiday cheer. Based on this month’s standout dress finds, the key elements are texture, color, and fabric. Art Deco influences were plenty on the fall runways, and drop-waist styles like Tory Burch’s deep red midi make for excellent party attire. ‘Tis also the season for autumnal textures in wool, velvet, jacquard—try a brocade number for an evening occasion, or pick up a sweater dress from either Me+Em or Proenza Schouler to wear throughout the winter. And for all fall weddings and holiday festivities on the horizon, there are simply too many good options—from Toteme to Staud—that will make you the best-dressed guest.

Whether you’re shopping for new essentials, vacation, or a destination wedding, these are November’s best dresses.

Cos reimagines the LBD with swishy godet panels, for a flattering, effortless silhouette. Pair it with flats for the office or kitten heels after dark. Did I mention this makes for a perfect cocktail dress?

The classic slip dress gets a romantic update in satin and Chantilly lace. An elegant choice for holiday soirées or the bride-to-be.

Toteme puts a fresh spin on the reverse collar trend with this pale pink silk dress. The draped silhouette makes for effortless office dressing.

A gala, a wedding, or an evening at the ballet? With its decadent embellishments and Art Deco allure, this dress is the epitome of 1920s glamour, fit for right now.

A favorite from Kallmeyer’s holiday capsule, this beaded mini is made for after parties. Style it with sheer tights and strappy sandals.

Fresh off Tory Burch’s fall 2026 runway, this drop-waist dress is ready for the holiday circuit. Pair with embellished heels for extra festive flair.

Two looks in one. Me+Em’s versatile set pairs a sleeveless turtleneck dress with a coordinating long-sleeve sweater. Drape the merino wool knit over your shoulders or tie it around your waist.

As temperatures dip, this textured bouclé dress offers a chic alternative to traditional winter knits. Finish the look with a ’90s-inspired tailored coat for understated elegance.

RSVP, yes! This dazzling purple dress makes a compelling case for bold color at upcoming weddings.

Decadent velvet without the decadent price tag? Zara delivers with this sumptuous crushed velvet gown. A true steal!

Taller Marmo’s red mini is a statement in itself. Pair it with sheer tights, strappy sandals, and a pouch for holiday events, or go bare-legged for a glamorous beach event.

Cooler temperatures are no reason to retire color. Consider this your invitation to embrace it. Fforme’s elegant take on the evening dress features a dropped waist, mock neckline, and sleeveless silhouette—all in a rich berry hue.

What’s a fall wardrobe without a knit dress? This under-$300 find from Banana Republic makes for a go-to in any wardrobe. Style it with knee-high boots for effortless cold-weather dressing.

Tory Burch sent this printed dress—in a trompe l’oeil pattern resembling tiger stripes—down the runway in two iterations: a delicate pastel jacquard and a rich purple version. With a fitted bodice that cascades into a handkerchief hemline, it’s a romantic silhouette that needs little extra to feel styled. A close-cut jacket and patent pumps should do the trick.

A knit dress is always a good idea. Simkhai’s ribbed iteration, accented with a delicate white trim, makes a subtle yet striking statement. Add a knee-high boot, a sweeping opera coat, and a chic clutch.

A dress that’ll get you multiple double-takes. This red maxi with a built-in cummerbund reimagines traditional black tie dress codes for a feminine-meets-masculine twist.

ICYMI: Jacquard is having a moment. This black V-neck dress, accented with a cummerbund sash, brings a polished edge to evening dressing. Even better? It’s under $300.

Conner Ives can do no wrong. Spaghetti straps, delicate pleats, and a vibrant color story—the dress is composed of four different printed vintage scarves—make this a vacation must-have, whether you’re spending Thanksgiving in Nayarita or St. Barths.

The shift is a forever classic and Posse’s silk-satin take is minimalist in the best way. Bring that less is more ethos to accessorizing with a simple pouch and drop earrings.

Emily Dawn Long—a CFDA 2026 runner-up—has a knack for intuiting what we want to wear before we do. This bright color-blocked midi is just one recent example.

Consider this sleeveless, funnel-neck knit dress a blank canvas for styling. Layer it over or under a long-sleeve knit (for extra warmth), throw on a sweeping shearling coat, then finish with flat boots. The possibilities are endless for cold-weather dressing.

You know the LBD, you (we hope) love the LBD. Play with proportions to give it a fresh look: a long duster coat, statement brooch, and polished loafers toughen up its feminine spirit.

Why yes, it’s Kallmeyer’s fall collection opening look: a creamy drop-waist style made from a silk charmeuse with caped armholes and a high funnel-neck. Follow the fall show’s styling notes and pair it with patent leather knee-highs–a pulled-back bun and minimal jewelry give the dress its well-deserved moment.

Maria McManus first introduced this dress in an off-white shade; this rich eggplant hue makes for a wonderful autumnal option.

Khaite’s chiffon maxi strikes the perfect balance between delicate and wearable. Give it heft by styling with a leather coat, tights, and strappy sandals.

Weddings or galas on the horizon? This strapless satin gown—as seen on supermodel Karlie Kloss, who wore it earlier this year for Taylor Swift’s wedding—works for either occasion.

Minimal, elegant, and endlessly versatile, this long-sleeve satin number is the kind of wardrobe staple that moves easily from desk job to after-hours plans. Dress it up with pumps or keep things understated with a flat—it looks sophisticated however your style it.

Kallmeyer’s Ivette dress is easily one of the season’s most talked-about dresses. With Art Deco influences leading the trend conversation, its embellished design feels especially on-trend.

Feathers, feathers, and more feathers! Whether you’re dressing for a special occasion or are a bride-to-be, this Loulou de Saison dress is designed to make an entrance. The drop-waist silhouette, adorned with feather embellishments around the hips, delivers just the right amount of drama. More is more!

Print enthusiasts, look no further than this floral maxidress from Banana Republic. Rendered in a rich persimmon print, the silhouette skims the body before flaring into a sweeping skirt. A romantic take on fall florals.

J.Crew’s cult-favorite rollneck sweater has officially entered its dress era. Just in time for sweater weather, its simple silhouette makes a strong case for becoming your new go-to. Style it with hosiery and loafers, then tie a colorful knit around your for an extra layer.

ICYMI: Purple is the color to own this season, and this violet maxi from Zara features an alluring open-back silhouette. Not quite ready to bare it all? Layer a lightweight top underneath, either in a neutral hue or a contrasting pop of color.

Caftans can be worn year-round—you just have to pick one in a more fall-friendly fabric. Taller Marmo’s long-sleeve is cut from double satin, with adjustable buttons that allows you to wear it in more ways than one—off-the-shoulder, single-shoulder, or or with a boat neckline.

Velvet chartreuse has never looked better, courtesy of Reformation x Alexa Chung, whose recent collaboration delivered one of the finest evening dresses of the month. Pair it with a satin bag and kitten heels.

This Staud dress creates the illusion of separates: A fitted black silhouette contrasts with a white draped skirt. A study that proves that opposites really do attract.

Meryll Rogge’s debut collection for Marni has officially dropped. The color-block mini is cut from one of the collection’s most memorable prints: a playful floral print that captures the house’s signature eccentricity. Pair with loafers and a long necklace.

For a quiet statement, consider this tea-length dress from Merlette, crafted from a rich butter yellow satin with ruched sleeves. On chillier days, add a faux-fur coat on top.

Altuzarra’s flutter-sleeve dress balances romance and structure, with delicate draping that creates soft movement. Save this for a special occasion.

Straight from the runway, this sleeveless knit turtleneck is a master class in sculptural dressing, crafted from a stretch rib that contours the body and falls to a handkerchief hem.

Who needs a necklace when the dress is the jewelry? Brandon Maxwell turns a V-neck dress into a work of art, with a beaded neckline that moves like fringe. An elegant, embellished option for an evening affair.

No dress roundup is complete without a little black dress. This off-the-shoulder option from Fforme is cut from a thick scuba fabric for a sculpted look. Complete the idea with strappy sandals and an embellished evening bag.

This Tory Burch runway dress was an editor favorite. Cut from jacquard in a slate blue and cherry-check motif, the color combination creates an optical illusion of a rich purple hue (one of this season’s trending hues). Two versatile details make it especially wearable: Both the necktie and belt are removable. Complete the look with fall boots.

To celebrate Vogue’s book club selection Sense and Sensibility, Vogue collaborated on a limited-edition nightgown inspired by Jane Austen's heroines. A nightgown that isn't exclusive to home can be styled with a trench and equestrian-inspired boots for an effortlessly romantic look.

Simon Miller's take on the slip dress is both elegant and flattering. This dress works season after season; it's the kind of piece that always makes an entrance, whether paired with boots or sleek mules.

CJR is known for its bold use of color, and this dress is no exception. Inspired by the work of Ettore Sottsass, the graphic polo maxi makes for a statement for any occasion. Dress it up with pumps or style it with flat boots for the weekend.

For upcoming weddings or formal events, look to this artful Tove dress. Playful yet sophisticated, the halter-neck silhouette is elevated by sculptural detailing. Finish off with strappy sandals for a polished finish.

For a minidress to wear this fall, opt for Khaite's Scarla dress. The modern skater silhouette, cut from delicate silk chiffon, feels romantic yet contemporary, making it an especially chic option for a bride-to-be.

Call it the ultimate party dress. The holiday season may still be a little off, but it’s never too early to plan your party wardrobe. This embellished Posse mini will make you the best-dressed guest.

Zara has collaborated with filmmaker Luca Guadagnino and production designer Stefano Baisi on a collection spanning from ready-to-wear to homeware. This scarf-draped dress strikes the perfect balance of elegance and ease.

Minimal yet statement-making, this Magda Butrym gray dress has an off-the-shoulder neckline and a fitted silhouette. A tonal floral appliqué adds a feminine, sculptural finish. Pair it with kitten heels and a clutch for an elegant evening look.

When your wardrobe is craving a dose of color, look to yellow. This H&M Studio dress is cut from a lightweight fabric with romantic ruffle detailing, making it an effortless choice for a warm-weather holiday or a destination wedding.

For a fall dress, look to this minidress inspired by the ’60s. Cut from a wool blend, this double-breasted dress is an ideal layering piece. Style it with a colorful turtleneck or button-down and add tights and boots for a milder fall day, or pair it with loafers.

Alaïa's approach to construction is like no other, creating some of the most flattering silhouettes around. Cut from velvet, this tank dress makes for an understated yet impactful evening option—a minimalist statement.

Maygel Coronel’s dress proves that simplicity can still make an impact. The elongated drop waist, fluid draping, and bubble hem give the silhouette a fresh modern feel.

A fall wardrobe essential, this long-sleeve satin dress is a versatile piece that works from nine to nine. Polished enough for the office and elegant enough for an evening, it transitions seamlessly from day to night.

A black dress is a timeless choice, and this Altuzarra option interprets the style for modern wardrobes with draping and an asymmetric knotted waist. A chic choice for fall weddings: Just add a kitten heel and a clutch.

A little lace, or in this case a lot, goes a long way. This runway favorite from Khaite strikes the perfect balance between romantic and edgy. Ground it with sleek black shoes.

Violet! Purple! Amethyst! However you choose to call them, deep shades of purple are having a serious moment. Style with something red—a clutch or heels, or even a bold lip—for contrast.

Toteme makes the kind of dresses you’ll want to wear on repeat—and this draped maxi is one of them. New in for the season (we’ve written about it in cream, red, and butter yellow), this rich olive hue feels just right for fall.

Casual meets sophisticated in this fresh-off-the-runway Prada mini, featuring a drawstring waist and cultural motifs at the hem. Wear it over pants for an unexpected look.

Cut from a thick satin, Róhe’s sculptural one-shoulder dress contours the body just so, and needs little in the way of styling to feel complete; simply finish with a tassel clutch and kitten heels. Also available as a top, it’s equally chic styled as a full ensemble for an important event.

Color is all everyone can talk about this season—and chartreuse is one of the It hues. This Taller Marmo dress with an integrated cape makes for a striking wedding guest option.

A knit dress streamlines getting ready on a cold, rainy day, and this colorful knit intarsia style by Celine–as seen in the Vogue Shopping print guide to fall–is one worth investing in. Wear it with loafers on a crisp fall day, then switch to knee-high boots for the winter.

The kind of dress Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy might have worn. This simple boatneck style from Zara is minimal yet endlessly versatile.

Tory Burch knows her way around a shirtdress, and this style–straight off the fall runway–comes with a removable necktie, allowing you to switch up the look depending on the occasion.

From weddings to galas, look to this Fforme drop waist dress in blue sapphire hue. Pair with strappy sandals and a sleek pouch bag.

&Other Stories’s pleated mock neck dress is an effortless style that can easily be transformed for any occasion. Pair it with blazers and loafers for the office or dress it up with pumps for evening events.

For a lace dress that’s feminine but not overly sweet, look no further than Maria McManus’s black satin midi. Style it with a button-down or cardigan knotted at the waist, then add an unexpected pop of color with either your shoes or your bag.

A rich blue hue and draped silhouette give this dress a modern take on the 1920s drop-waist silhouette. Dress it up with heels for evening or ground it with loafers for an uptown-meets-downtown approach.

The nightie was a summer favorite, and for fall, Dôen gives it a polished update in a maxi silhouette with silk and lace trimmings. The result is a romantic yet refined style that works just as well at the office as it does for cocktails.

The LBD for minimalists comes courtesy of Toteme, who’ve crafted a short sleeve style from a bonded scuba crepe with darted seams for a subtly sculptural silhouette. Pair with tights and patent heels.

Khaite’s new fall collection has arrived, and this layered maxi, crafted from a sheer silk organza, is a standout. An elegant bustle detail at the back adds unexpected drama.

You’re not imaging it: Purple is one of the season’s standout shades and Toteme’s scarf dress is one of our favorite renditions. Finish with contrasting red or lemon hues for a jaunty color story.

Florals aren’t just reserved for spring. Ulla Johnson’s long-sleeve turtleneck dress makes the print feel autumnal. Pair with boots for this transitional period.

Kallmeyer’s Nala dress has Vogue bride written all over it. Keep the finishing touches pared-back with drop earrings and sleek white shoes.

Straight from Proenza Schouler’s fall runway is this artfully printed dress that’s great for any number of September occasions on your calendar. Pair it with kitten heels and a leather jacket for dinner out with friends, or with boots on cooler days.

Alaïa knows how to celebrate the female form, and this maxi from Pieter Mulier’s final collection for the house does just that. Crafted from ultra-soft merino, it’s also available in a zesty chartreuse, and classic black.

Not your typical minimalist ’90s slip. This olive-green version gets a romantic update with intricate lace trimming.

Whether you’re heading somewhere warm this month or simply leaning into fall’s version of artful bohemian dressing, a caftan always delivers. Easy and elegant, all you need is a long pendant and some chunky bangles to style it out.

COS reimagines the gather dress with a twisted detail at the front for asymmetric like draping. A no-brainer 9-5 option that needs minimal styling.

The Best Holiday Cocktails, According to Eater Editors

📅 Nov 22, 2022  |  Category: Entertainment  |  Read Source →

Don’t let cocktails fall by the wayside in the flurry of holiday dinner prep — these drinks make the party

In the endless iterating that goes into devising a menu for a holiday dinner, there’s one finishing touch that really makes or breaks the vibe: the drinks. The wine and beer will, of course, flow — at these festive events, a bottle of Champagne or sparkling rose is likely to make an appearance — and it’s easy enough to throw together a gin and tonic or screwdriver. But nothing makes a holiday gathering feel chic, totally put together, gloriously intentional, like a batch cocktail, made-to-order martini, or gussied-up punch.

Now, we all have our preferences when it comes to strength, spirit, and format. The host’s bandwidth is also a consideration; do you want to make a lot of one thing, or tailor your options to your guests’ preferences? Those questions are for you to answer, but our staff is here to help by providing this rundown of six tried, vetted, and loved drinks to make at your own celebration.

Below, find Eater editor-approved recipes for cocktails that will add the most festive of feelings to every holiday gathering.

Stack more, spend less. Amazon Grocery lets you spend less on all the people who eat your food. Shop Amazon for everyday low prices on groceries and get free same-day delivery with Prime.

I host a holiday potluck with a core group of friends in December, and one of my favorite potential additions is whatever punch that drinks columnist M. Carrie Allan is cooking up over at the Washington Post. A favorite from 2022 was a meringue-topped citrus punch, featuring blood orange, Aperol, and a dramatic meringue topping. Said topping adds undeniable flair and drama to the presentation, but if you’re daunted by the idea, the punch itself is still a festive, not-too-sweet drink to serve, celebrating winter citrus. —Missy Frederick, editorial director, dining

Meaghan Dorman’s modern classic is a favorite year-round, but there’s something about the holidays that calls for Scotch. No shade to the nog freaks, but the subtly spiced sour is a pleasant counterpoint to the onslaught of holiday food and beverage maximalism. No need to break out the single malt either, your dusty bottle of Dewars or Monkey Shoulder will do just fine. —Allison Hamlin, director of network development

The French 75 — the effervescent classic cocktail made with gin, Champagne, and lemon — is already one of my easy-drinking favorites, and I like it even better in punch form, accented with an aesthetically pleasing ice block of cheery lemon slices. What makes it 77 instead of 75? The substitution of St-Germain (or any elderflower liqueur) for simple syrup, adding just a tiny touch of herbal complexity. It’s perfect for New Year’s Eve, but just as refreshing at Thanksgiving or any other holiday table where you want something light and zesty. —Hilary Pollack, deputy editor

As the de facto cook for Thanksgiving, I like to keep the drinks options simple so I can focus on food prep. This cocktail recipe requires only two ingredients, doesn’t require pre-batching, and is easy enough for people to pour on their own. I also like how it uses Basque cider, which is drier than the typical ciders, so it’s not too sweet while still tapping into that cozy fall feeling —Rayna Rossitto, editor, branded content

I grew up guzzling Broguiere’s eggnog, but I love the more tropical combination of rich, creamy coconut milk, rum, and cinnamon in coquito; the Puerto Rican holiday cocktail was first described to me as “eggnog, if it went on vacation,” and I haven’t looked back since. This version is by bartender Shannon Ponche, and gets extra dressed up in spice for the holidays with the addition of a homemade cinnamon simple syrup, a woody, nutty oloroso sherry, and a splash of spiced Braulio. —Francky Knapp, staff writer

There are two schools of thought on a post-dinner drink: You could go for a bracing digestif to “aid digestion,” or you could indulge in a liquid dessert that swaddles you in sugar, fat, and everything nice. I’m notoriously bad at decision making, so I tend to split the difference with an eggy flip tinged with something bitter. Together, a whole egg and syrup (in this case honey syrup) build a comforting base, while an entire 1.5 ounces of cocktail bitters (as opposed to the usual dash or two) ensure you don’t entirely fall asleep in your glass. Angostura is a great option, delivering some classic holiday spice, but any style of cocktail bitters would probably work, as would an amaro. Dry shaking (shaking the liquid ingredients without ice) is key to achieving a frothy texture, and don’t forget the half-ounce of whiskey, which punches up the rest of the flavors. —Nick Mancall-Bitel, editor

Several members of my husband’s family are Manhattan drinkers, so I expect that my decision to serve the Grandfather cocktail during Thanksgiving appetizers will be a hit. It’s a riff on the classic drink with a hint of fall, courtesy of the addition of Applejack, an apple brandy. It’s smooth and well-balanced. It’s also quite boozy, so I’ll probably look for a slightly lower-proof option to tide us over after that initial round. I’ve had success with a bourbon and ginger ale bar (with various sodas and mixers) in the past, as well as Smitten Kitchen’s fall sangria; maybe this year we’ll go with her (okay, still pretty boozy) apple cider Old Fashioneds. —Missy Frederick, cities director

19 Pumpkin Purée Recipes From Cake to Pie

📅 Oct 11, 2022  |  Category: Other  |  Read Source →

As soon as fall arrives, canned pumpkin purée earns a permanent spot in the pantry. After all, it’s shelf-stable and can be turned into a trillion recipes, sweet and savory alike. Just be sure you’re using plain canned pumpkin purée, not pumpkin pie filling, which already contains sugar and spices.

Some recipes, like our Pumpkin Spice Crumb Cake, call for just half a can, while others, like Weeknight Pumpkin Chili, use the whole thing. But if you have leftover pumpkin purée hanging out in the fridge, consider it a good thing—it just means another pumpkin recipe is on the horizon. And if you’ve gone the extra mile to make pumpkin purée from fresh pumpkins, you overachiever, check the recipe before swapping it in: Homemade purée can be wetter than canned. So grab a scarf and let’s take a stroll, shall we?

These pumpkin pancakes are tall, light, and warmly spiced, with tangy buttermilk and fresh ginger in the batter. Top with maple syrup–spiked butter and crunchy pecans for a breakfast worth getting out of bed for.

As if pumpkin muffins with a crunchy pepita streusel weren’t enough, these have a hidden surprise: a pocket of sweetened cream cheese. They’re part breakfast, part cheesecake, and entirely worth getting out of bed for.

Tart cranberries punctuate these tender pumpkin scones, while a sprinkle of raw sugar adds a crisp finish. Serve them warm with the accompanying cinnamon-maple butter, which you can make up to four days ahead.

Part pancake, part custard, this Dutch baby comes with a bonus pumpkin purée recipe: ¼ cup goes into the batter, and the rest of the can becomes a silky, spiced pumpkin butter to spread on top. Leftover butter is excellent on toast.

Fresh ginger gives this super-moist pumpkin bread a little kick, while pumpkin seeds add crunch. The secret to its tender crumb? Extra-virgin olive oil. And don’t skip the salted maple butter for slathering on every slice.

Read more: What Kind of Olive Oil Should You Use in Olive Oil Cake?

Sweet, mellow pumpkin and sharp, salty cheddar are a perfect match in this hearty strata. Assemble it the day before to let the bread soak up the savory custard, then bake until golden and crisp on top.

A pumpkin spice latte you don’t need to leave the house for. Unlike many café versions, this one actually contains pumpkin purée. Don’t have an espresso machine? Swap in strong coffee instead.

This tender, deeply spiced pumpkin cake comes together without a stand mixer and gets a generous swoop of tangy cream cheese frosting. A drizzle of maple syrup is optional but highly encouraged.

This plush chocolate-pumpkin cake draws inspiration from Mexican chocolate, with cinnamon and a pinch of cayenne for warmth. The pumpkin glaze doubles down on the seasonal flavor.

With nearly as much brown sugar streusel as plush pumpkin cake, this New York–style crumb cake takes its topping seriously. If there is a more comforting afternoon snack, we need not know it.

Cinnamon-spiced pumpkin cake wraps around walnut-studded cream cheese frosting in a pretty spiral. The batter comes together in one bowl, but be sure to roll the cake while it’s still warm to prevent cracks.

Pumpkin and chocolate cake batters combine for a dramatic marbled effect in this striking Bundt cake. A glossy chocolate ganache finishes the job. It looks like a project, but you don’t even need a mixer.

Classic crumb cake meets chewy, bouncy mochi in this pumpkin-spiced mash-up. Sweet rice flour gives the cake its distinctive texture, while a buttery pecan streusel adds crunch. It’s particularly good for sharing at Friendsgiving.

Silky filling, flaky crust, a whisper of spice: This is pumpkin pie done right. And there’s no need to roast and purée a fresh pumpkin—our favorite canned variety delivers the consistency we’re after.

With its deeply browned top and creamy, pumpkin-spiced center, this Basque cheesecake looks impressive but skips the fussy water bath. No crust required, either. A full can of pumpkin purée goes into the filling.

The caramelized notes of bourbon and tang of sour cream balance this classic Gourmet dessert. Chopped pecans give the graham cracker crust a little extra crunch.

Can’t choose between pumpkin pie and cheesecake? These maple-sweetened bars make a pretty convincing argument for having both. Swirls of creamy cheesecake and spiced pumpkin filling make them especially handsome on a dessert platter.

Imagine a pumpkin pie with pecan pie’s best feature—obviously, the candied nut topping. A splash of rye whiskey adds a little malty complexity to this two-for-one Thanksgiving dessert.

This positively fluffy pumpkin pie gets a little nutty depth from tahini, whose toasty, slightly bitter flavor balances the sweet pumpkin filling. Whipped cream keeps things light and airy.

This autumnal riff on Puerto Rican flan de queso gets its exceptionally velvety texture from cream cheese. Pumpkin purée and warm spices bring the seasonal flavor, while a glossy caramel topping makes it hard to resist.

What’s more satisfying than cracking through that caramelized sugar topping? Finding a luscious, pumpkin-spiced custard underneath. This recipe uses an entire can of purée, and you can finish the sugar under the broiler if you don’t own a kitchen torch.

Everything you love about classic tiramisu, with the warming spices of a pumpkin spice latte. Ladyfingers dipped in bourbon-spiked espresso alternate with creamy pumpkin mascarpone filling. Make it ahead and dust with cinnamon and cocoa just before serving.

This streamlined recipe turns three hard-working ingredients—curry paste, coconut milk, and pumpkin purée—into a cozy, flavorful soup in just 30 minutes. Proof that a pantry dinner doesn’t have to feel like a compromise.

A whole can of pumpkin purée becomes a silky pasta sauce with garlic, Parmesan, and a kick of chile. Just the thing for a weeknight when you want something comforting without committing to an afternoon of cooking.

A full can of pumpkin purée becomes the sauce—no simmering required—for these cheesy black bean enchiladas. A quick turn under the broiler melts and browns the cheese; lime and crunchy pepitas finish the job.

A full can of pumpkin purée adds richness, body, and an autumnal hue to this speedy chili without making it taste like pumpkin pie. Ground beef, beans, and savory spices keep the flavors firmly in chili territory.

Adding pumpkin purée to Bolognese might not seem obvious, but it gives the sauce rich body without hours of simmering. Cooking it with tomato paste brings out its nutty, caramelized flavor.

Rolling the filled noodles into spirals adds a whimsical touch and ensures every bite has the perfect balance of spinach-ricotta, tender pasta, and creamy pumpkin sauce.

Canned pumpkin purée gives no-knead focaccia a golden hue, subtle sweetness, and plush crumb. Finish with rosemary and flaky salt (both optional, both recommended), and serve with a dish of olive oil for dipping.

A Good Pair of Pickleball Shoes Can Help Improve Your Game. Here Are Our Top Picks.

📅 Jul 11, 2022  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Improve your game with the latest pickleball-ready shoes.

PICKLEBALL IS A fun way to stay fit, which is especially true if you have the proper gear. This ensures you can make the most of all your matches, which starts from the ground up. Buying a pair of pickleball shoes is one of the smartest investments you can make in your game. Unlike your pickleball paddle, your pickleball shoes have a much more direct relationship to your health. Two of the most important factors to consider are traction and stability.

Like tennis shoes, pickleball shoes need to handle quick movements in all types of directions. That means you want strong outsoles with responsive tread patterns and a midsole structure that can handle fast-twitch lateral movements. Lateral stability is super important since it can help prevent common pickleball injuries to ankles or knees, so it’s more important for them to have a wider base and a stiff lower structure to provide this kind of maximum stability. Our guide to the best pickleball shoes will set you up with the right kind of shoe for enhancing performance while hopefully reducing the odds of rolling an ankle or spraining a knee.

DOWNLOAD OUR ULTIMATE PICKLEBALL WORKOUT PLAN PDF

The Rush Pro Ace Pickleball is designed for both indoor and outdoor court surfaces and has a 4D Support Chassis for controlled pivot movements and stability. When we tested it out, The Pickler held tough through all the wear and tear.

The rubber drag pad has helped protect tearing on the end of the toe box, and the cushioned midsole helps keep high foot arches comfortable. The Pickler even has a rebound-like effect when making fast-twitch movements, which makes sense because of how close in construction the shoe is to Pro Ace Tennis Shoe—Wilson's top-selling model for tennis. The rebound of the shoe alone isn't going to make you a better player, but we do believe it helps promote staying on your toes more during play, especially when it comes to getting into a firefight against opponents.

The performance on this shoe is superb, and the style promises a clean look that's suitable for wearing in a country club environment. The comfort of the shoe—namely the supportive arch and cushioned padding around the tongue and ankle—became the final selling point to deem these the best pickleball shoes overall in 2026.

If you’re getting into pickleball for the first time, you don’t want to spend close to $200 just to find out it isn't for you. A great affordable pickleball shoe can help you there—it’s also a great option for those who simply like to budget, too. Enter the second iteration of the Asics Gel-Renma pickleball shoes. A stellar shoe for under $100.

Loaded with similar tech and materials you’ll find in Asics pro-level models, this pair uses a synthetic leather overlay for solid durability as well as its signature Trusstic tech, which helps to enhance stability. To help create a shoe that’s well-balanced for all directional movements, it uses a wrap-up outsole with flex grooves for increased flexibility, and a wider gauge. As Winn notes, "Asics has skyrocketed to the top over the last few years," and this pair is one affordable, high-performance pair.

You might be surprised to find K-Swiss at the top of the pickleball shoe market, but the brand has quietly been creating trusted game-ready models for all types of price points. We've come to find the Express Light as one of the top supportive and strong pickleball shoes money can buy.

Two main features of this shoe stood out when testing: the 180-degree Plantar Support Chassis and the DURAWRAP cover to help combat toe dragging. The support chassis worked great at providing a secure feeling while playing, giving ample support for high arches and preventing feet from twisting and rolling inside the shoe—even when they go hot and sweaty. The DURAWRAP cover is the outsole material used to combat abrasion and toe-dragging. The cover is definitely hard alright, and so it's nice to know you have this strong outer shell over the cushioned mesh that feels oh-so-good on the feet.

The shoes do fit quite snugly, so consider potentially going up a half size on this shoe. The design is unique, and fun with multiple colorways. It's not the fastest shoe, but it provides great durability and support. This is a well-balanced model you can play outside in for long periods of time.

If you’re looking for one lightweight, serious pair of pickleball shoes that can also handle the wear and tear of aggressive game play, the second version of the Viper Courts are definitely the way to go.This go around features a revamped upper that makes them even more durable than the previous gen, while remaining just as breathable and potentially even more comfortable (at least popular opinion says, according to reviewers).

These low tops feature quite the supportive feel with their EVA insoles and responsive foam in the midsoles that are topped off with Goodyear Gold compound soles that can take all the quick cuts and bursts you’ll find yourself doing every game. Plus, they’re versatile enough for the other two big racket sports of tennis and Padel.

New Balance takes the cake when it comes to shoes for those in need of a little extra stability. Both instructors we talked to agree that New Balance always delivers on comfort, support, and above all, stability. Between the precise underfoot cushioning, superior durability, or the FuelCell foam, the elements all come together to form a thoughtful design.

"They're well-made, so they last a long time and are very comfortable," Winn says. Armstrong also adds, "Looking around and asking a few of our senior players, [the New Balances] seem to be a fan favorite." At the end of the day, comfort and stability are the leading factors in selecting a shoe for seniors, both of which this shoe excels in, according to Armstrong.

Babolat doesn't just make stellar tennis racquets; the brand's tennis shoes are in a league of its own. With a soft upper and ventilated mesh, the SFX 4 delivers comfort and breathability in each wear. Babolat doubles down on the comfort with an OrthoLite insole that molds to the shape of your foot. A premium cushioning system absorbs shock in landings, which is super important for comfort and keeping your knees feeling good after a match. The shape and composition of the materials in the sole are segmented into nine key pressure points to deliver maximum responsiveness.

Armstrong also recommends these shoes for beginners. "In my experience, beginners need to look for something that may not require a huge investment, but also provides all the benefits needed to play tennis comfortably and safely," he says. "Generally, the shoes that are in a new player's price range and then feel the best, are the best shoes for them."

Pickleball is a social event and if you want a pair that can go from the courts to drinks afterwards, these Pickle Pro is our choice for sure. With their modern design and streamlined look, you could probably toss on a pair of slacks while wearing these and get away with it. I have worn them out in public running errands multiple times already and have even gotten several compliments on them, they’re that sharp.

Aesthetics aside, these shoes can still hold their own on the courts thanks to their solid design. For starters, these are darn comfortable with their OrthoLite foam midsoles that make them quite plush for a pair of pickleball shoes. Comfy as they are, they are quite tough too, which stems from the Duralast high-density soles that grips well on all court surfaces, but, it does mean they take a bit to break in from my experience. While I wouldn’t necessarily choose them for ultra competitive games, for a stylish and casual game, these are an absolute winner.

The Barricade is a go-to for all training sessions and matches for players who prioritize comfort. When shopping for shoes, Armstrong says, "Players have different criteria as to what makes a shoe great. Personally, I want something that is durable, supportive but not too bulky, and comfortable." Armstrong, who teaches/plays almost every day of the week, needs something that feels good on his notoriously aching Achilles tendon. Adidas makes this pair that does all of this, and are even a favorite of Armstrong's father (who tore his Achilles a few years ago) because of their unrivaled comfort.

Wonder why? It might have something to do with the shoe's foam Geofit Sensepods to securely lock in the heel, a cushioned Bounce midsole, and asymmetrical laces to help guard against the effects of foot drag. There's also a sustainability component, with 50 percent of the yarn in the upper being recycled.

If your the type of player who loves to chase down every shot, you’re going to need a shoe that can keep up. That means you’re going to want a pair that flexes and moves with your natural foot strike, allowing you to stay light on the balls of your feet. One of the best in the game right now that allows just those types of movement patterns are the CourtStrike Pro 2.0s from Selkirk.

Thanks to their 3D printing, you get a secure shoe with excellent lateral stability and a super responsive EVA midsole that helps to drastically improve you're reaction time. This allows you to stay explosive and react at will.

This 2.0 model features better, more durable rubber, extra material protection along the bottom of the laces for increased longevity, and multiple layered cushioning for a springier step. If you’re on a budget, you may want to opt for another pair on our list, but if you want one of the most versatile pairs around, just get these.

Pickleball shoes need to provide support, so buying the lightest shoe possible is not the smartest move. When buying a lightweight shoe (say, under 10 ounces) there's likely to be some sacrifice in support or stability. The trick? Stick to pickleball-specific shoes first. You can also consider tennis shoes and cross-trainers due to their similar support-first construction. Avoid featherlight running shoes that are built for a different type of movement.

Mesh is the most common and best material to look for in the upper of a pickleball shoe. However, like weight, you don't necessarily need the most breathable mesh possible. Some pickleball shoes sacrifice breathability to boost abrasion resistance, and to help keep your foot secure (like limiting your foot rolling and turning inside the shoe).

When it comes to the outsole, look for a shoe that has a strong rubber pattern that will help grip surfaces and reduce the odds of slipping when turning your feet. Some pickleball shoes pay greater attention to tread pattern, which can help provide a feeling of better grip on a court. Outsole will largely come down to personal preference, as most are constructed about the same.

When looking at the midsole, aim for a shoe that has supportive cushioning (like EVA foam) and keeps a relatively low profile. Prioritizing a midsole with too much cushioning could lead you to a shoe that sits high (like a Hoka running shoe), thus leading to a less responsive design, which could potentially lead to a greater chance of rolling an ankle when making fast turns on the court.

I have been fortunate enough to rock quite a few pairs of pickleball shoes over the past few years. Having played on multiple surfaces, I’ve learned a few things about what to look for when selecting a pair. I also partnered with our other writers and editors at Men's Health to help select the best pickleball shoes we’ve tested in the past few years, available. We’ve compiled a guide to the best all-day play, taking great note of each shoe's stability, durability, weight, and price point. Special consideration was taken into account for pickleball shoes that had excellent traction and stability since those two qualities are the most important in a pickleball shoe.

There is a lot of crossover from effective tennis shoes to pickleball shoes. So we also spoke to experts like Life Time Galleria Tennis Leader Gary Armstrong (who has been playing tennis for 36 years and has been an instructor for 17 years) and Life Time Charlotte Tennis Leader Eric Winn (who has been a tennis coach for 24 years and still plays in the 5.0 USTA leagues) to get their takes on the best tennis shoes for men. With minimal differences, some of their picks made it to this guide.

If you're someone who's going to play pickleball once or twice for recreation, then you could get away with a low-profile running shoe. But if you're expecting to play any more than that, we strongly recommend buying a proper pair of pickleball shoes.

The reason we don't recommend wearing just any type of running shoe is that running shoes are made for forward motion, so there's often less emphasis on reinforcing the shoe for side-to-side movements. Running shoes also have less structure and stability than what you want in a pickleball shoe, as the running styles these days are made to be as lightweight and breathable as possible (with high cushioned stacks), which means less focus on overall support.

So, to be clear, you should steer from wearing running shoes for pickleball if you expect to play the game on a regular basis. A proper pickleball shoe is a smart investment that will help give you traction and stability while greatly decreasing the chance of rolling an ankle or spraining a knee.

What Happened When Paul Scholes Came Out of Retirement, Aged 43, For Royton Town

📅 Jan 25, 2022  |  Category: Sports  |  Read Source →

Rob is senior football editor at GiveMeSport, with over 15 years experience covering sport in various capacities since graduating from the University of Gloucestershire in 2008 with a degree in journalism. A childhood obsession for all things football developed into a career writing about the beautiful game, initially producing content for clients including Luton Town Football Club and the PGMOL. His first big interviews were with Premier League referees Howard Webb and Michael Oliver in 2009. He then spent four years producing written content for a betting website, mainly focusing on football, and was there to cover various games and tournaments including the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012. Rob joined GiveMeSport in 2013 (initially as a sub-editor before becoming a senior writer and then senior editor in 2020) and has covered countless football matches and other sporting events, interviewed various high-profile figures including Rio Ferdinand, Peter Crouch and Theo Walcott, and written well over 10,000 articles during that time. Rob has played a key role in GiveMeSport's coverage of the World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, plus Euro 2016, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, along with many Champions League finals. While football is Rob's area of expertise, he has also covered a wide range of other sports during his time at GiveMeSport including boxing, tennis and darts, as well as the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Olympic Games.

Imagine turning up to play for your semi-professional team on a Saturday afternoon and spotting Paul Scholes lacing up his boots for the opponents. Your first thought would be: ‘Wait a minute, is that Pau… no, can’t be!'

Stockport Georgians’ players experienced this in September 2018 when Scholes, in his early 40s at the time, came out of retirement to help out his son’s team. Royton Town, who were competing in the 11th tier of English football, managed to convince the Manchester United legend to pull on their maroon strip for one game only.

They were short on players and told their opponents that they were bringing in a 43-year-old dad to help out. Little did Stockport Georgians know that the unnamed father in question was one of the greatest midfielders in the history of English football.

Having retired in 2013, the appearance for Royton Town was Scholes' first bit of competitive action on a football pitch in five years. It was also officially recorded as the 500th appearance of his professional career. A couple of videos of the former midfielder in action were posted to social media at the time.

Even at 43 in a semi-pro game, Scholesy was still prepared to fly into a 50/50 tackle. However, the presence of a former England international and one of the best English footballers of all time wasn’t enough to prevent Royton slumping to a 1-0 defeat.

If you were part of the Stockport Georgians’ team that afternoon, you’d surely mention that you beat a team containing one of the greatest midfielders in Premier League history at every available opportunity. Despite the defeat, Royton manager Mark Howard had plenty of praise for Scholes.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Paul Scholes played 713 games for Manchester United, winning 11 Premier League titles in the process to become one of the most decorated players in football history.

Despite losing the game 1-0, Howard was very happy with what he saw from Scholes and credited him for "raising the level of those around him by 10-15 per cent” - including that of his own son, Arron. The manager spoke to BBC Sport about the game afterwards and explained why the Englishman had offered to play:

"We had eight or nine of our senior players missing and Paul said he'd be happy to help out if we were ever short as his son Arron plays for us. It's great for the league. Opponents don't want to look stupid in front of him."

The gaffer wasn't the only one grateful for Scholes' efforts and helping out in the game. Royton chairman Gary Leeming also praised the legendary midfielder, one of the greatest Premier League players of all time, following his cameo.

Following Howard's comments, Royton's chairman also got in on the action and publicly praised Scholes. He credited the former United man for boosting the team's attendance for the match and revealed that he'd occasionally been training with the side prior to playing for them anyway and had proven he was still very good despite his age.

"Usually, these sort of games attract 40 or 50 people but there were a lot more there when word got out that he was playing. I can't imagine Stockport Georgians have ever had so many people on their car park.

"We were down to the bare bones. He's 43 now but he's still got that magic wand and he was absolutely fantastic for us. He obviously has a lot of media commitments but he occasionally trains with us when he can and is still a great player."

Class truly is permanent. It's not what Scholes is used to, having shone on the grandest stages such as the Premier League and the Champions League, but when you truly love the beautiful game, it doesn't matter where you are - as long as you've got a ball.

13 Retailers You Never Knew Would Recycle Your Old Stuff

📅 Jan 12, 2022  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

100+ Most Unique and Practical Gifts 🎁 for Homeowners and DIYers

Updated Nov 10, 2026 11:43 AM EST

As consumers, we create a massive amount of waste, filling up landfills with all of the products we’ve used and thrown away. While most people have a recycling bin along with their trash bin, they might not realize that many stores they frequent offer exceptional recycling programs for the items that can’t go in the recycling container.

These major retailers have robust recycling programs that can refurbish and reuse your old clothes, smartphones, rechargeable batteries, or furniture. And, for items that aren’t reusable, the retailers partner with recycling companies that can break them down into their base components to create a variety of other products.

“These sort of recycling programs are of huge importance,” says Paula Napolitano, product sales manager at Wisetek, a major Ireland-based distributor of refurbished and recycled electronics. “Last year there were around 59 million metric tons of e-waste generated globally, which is hugely impacting the environment. If large amounts of old electronics are allowed to build up in landfills, they can eventually begin to leach toxic materials into the soil, which may seriously harm the surrounding environment,” Napolitano says.

While lowering the impact you have on the local landfill is reason enough to hand off unwanted furniture, bedsheets, tablets, or rechargeable batteries to these retailers, you might be surprised to know that many of these companies offer additional incentives in the form of coupons, gift cards, and trade-in deals. Ahead, learn more about some of the top retailers who will take your unwanted stuff.

The big-box appliance and electronics giant is a leader in recycling, reusing, or repurposing, to the tune of 2.7 billion pounds of e-waste and appliances since 2009. You can drop off old electronics like computers, smartphones, radios, and more at any of Best Buy’s more than 1,000 locations and receive special promotions off certain products in the store. You can even earn gift cards for those items that still have value. Best Buy will also haul old TVs, fitness equipment, and appliances away for a nominal fee when you buy new ones.

“You can recycle up to three items per household per day,” says Alejandra Valeriano, public relations representative for Best Buy. “For $199.99, we’ll haul away and recycle up to a total of two large products (including TVs, major appliances, all-in-one computers and monitors), along with an unlimited number of select smaller products,” Valeriano says. Best Buy partners with Electronic Recyclers International, which breaks down electronics into materials that can be repurposed for use in everything from fiber optic cables to airplanes.

Few retailers have as robust a recycling program as The Home Depot. Consumers can access their comprehensive recycling web page that explains how to recycle everything from plastic plant pots to florescent tube lights. The company partners with nonprofit recycling company The Battery Network (formerly Call2Recycle) to recycle a variety of battery types, including those for power tools, EVs, and e-bikes. In 2024, The Home Depot recycled approximately 1 million pounds of rechargeable batteries. The retailer also collects plastic bags for composite manufacturer Trex, which uses them to make fencing and decking.

Not only will Staples recycle your old office supplies and electronics, they’ll pay you for it. Since 2012, Staples has recycled nearly 188 million pounds of technology. “Staples wants to make recycling easier for everyone across the U.S.,” says Mike Sauchuk, senior director of recycling and sustainability of Staples. “There are many items out there that we use every day that can be recycled, but it can be challenging to find a place to recycle them. That’s where Staples steps in. We offer free recycling for many hard-to-recycle items like technology, writing instruments, phone cases, and more. There’s no more waiting for your town’s local recycling day or event. At Staples, it’s recycling day every day.”

Through the Staples Rewards program, you can earn $5 back in rewards when you recycle tech and $2 back on every recycled ink or toner cartridge brought to one of the store’s more than 1,000 locations. In addition, the retailer will take unwanted electronics and worn-out rechargeable batteries for free.

Like other retailers, Walmart will take used cell phones, Bluetooth speakers, laptops, gaming consoles, tablets, and other devices through its trade-in program. Simply input info about the device on the Walmart website, get an offer for it, then ship it for free via FedEx or UPS Ground using a preprinted label. You receive an instant Walmart gift card for your efforts.

The presence of mercury, cadmium, lithium, and lead in car batteries ranks these vital components of cars and trucks among the more harmful products for the environment. Advance Auto Parts knows this, and therefore the company offers a nice incentive for bringing in your old battery once it dies. Take the worn-out battery to any Advance store and you’ll get a $10 gift card, which you can put toward the cost of a new battery or anything else in the store. The old batteries are then used to manufacture new ones.

While Apple’s products might be on the more expensive side when it comes to consumer electronics, they hold some of their value. That’s because the company makes it easy to cash in on that old iPhone, iPad, Macbook, or Apple Watch by allowing owners of the devices to trade their electronics in at an Apple Store or online. In return, Apple gives the customer store credit (Apple will also recycle other brands of electronics for free).

If the device is in good shape, it will be refurbished and resold. Those that can’t be reused go to one of Apple’s recycling partners, where they are broken down and recycled. Many iPhones end up with Daisy, Apple’s disassembly robot, which is designed to recover a device’s usable parts.

Habitat for Humanity’s ReStore has more than 900 locations nationwide, all of which will take appliances, furniture, various household items, and even building materials. Habitat then resells these items in its store and uses the proceeds to build affordable homes for families. “New and gently used items donated to a Habitat ReStore are resold to the community at a fraction of retail prices and help to support Habitat for Humanity’s vision of a world where everyone has a decent place to live,” says Jared Williams, communications manager at Habitat for Humanity International.

According to Williams, “Habitat ReStores tend to accept both new and gently used household items and building materials, which can include a wide variety of products.” He adds that donations come from all kinds of sources, “from neighbors completing home projects to restaurants after a remodel.” Habitat might not offer you a gift card for your stuff, but you can take tax deductions for your donations, since Habitat is a nonprofit organization.

RELATED: Don’t Throw Your Old Christmas Lights in the Trash—Do This Instead

Ever wonder where the used products Amazon sells come from? The online retailing behemoth accepts your old electronics and devices, including Bluetooth speakers and headphones, home security devices, wireless routers, and gaming systems. The company will even reward you with gift cards for gently used electronics that it can refurbish and resell. Amazon also takes some products that are no longer functioning. The company will recycle a variety of electronic devices for free, even covering the cost of shipping them to Amazon via UPS.

Bedding, unmatched socks, old T-shirts—clothing retailer H&M will take all linens as part of the company’s recycling program. Since 2013, H&M has collected more than 172,000 tons of textiles. The items were either cleaned and reused as second-hand clothing, turned into other products such as cleaning rags, or recycled into materials like insulation. When you drop off a bag of used clothing at H&M, the company will give you a coupon toward your next purchase at their store.

More than 1 billion HP ink and toner cartridges have been recycled by customers through the company’s HP Planet Partners program. The program aims to give a second life to HP’s end-of-life equipment and printing supplies and to reduce the environmental impact of electronic waste and greenhouse gas emissions. Simply drop off your HP ink and toner supplies at a location near you, mail them back, or request a pickup if you have a large quantity of supplies to give back.

Calling all coffee enthusiasts! If you own a Nespresso machine, you might be familiar with the company’s recycling program. Fill a Nespresso recycling bag (available for free at any Nespresso store) with your used capsules and drop them off at one of the 122,000-plus collection points around the world. The aluminum from the pods is recycled into items such as bicycles, computers, and soda cans, while the used coffee grounds create compost or green energy.

Kroger recognizes that most shoppers throw out plastic grocery bags and packaging after shopping, so they’ve put a special system in place for customers to take your discarded grocery bags and packaging and recycle them responsibly. The retail giant provides convenient drop-off bins to recycle plastic. The grocery chain has recycled more than 180 million pounds of plastic and aims to eliminate single-use plastic grocery bags in all of their stores by 2025.

Williams-Sonoma has a variety of initiatives dedicated to creating a more circular economy. The company works with donation programs like Good360 to give away returned and unsold products to local nonprofit organizations and others. They are also exploring rental and resale business models to give a second life to products like bedding, curtains, throws, pillows, linens, and more.

10 Best Eye Cream for Dark Circles of 2026, According to Experts

📅 Jan 06, 2022  |  Category: Lifestyle  |  Read Source →

While some people appreciate the natural look of a shadowy under-eye, many of us hope to find a solution—which is where the best eye cream for dark circles comes in. “Not all eye creams are created equal, because not all eye problems are equal,” says board-certified dermatologist Dr. Shereene Idriss. “When a person is looking to treat dark circles, the question is: Why do you have dark circles?”

The answer is different for everyone. For some people, it’s pigment, which can be genetic or the result of tiredness. For others, the skin under the eyes is so thin that the blood vessels underneath show through as a bluish or purple cast. If you’re experiencing puffiness, that can cast its own shadow, especially in the morning. Finally, as we get older, a little volume loss where the lower lid meets the cheek can make the whole area look darker than it really is.

That’s why when it comes to your eye cream, the ingredient list matters. Vitamin C, niacinamide and licorice root are good picks for pigment. Formulas that include retinol and peptides help thin skin look firmer and less see-through over time, and caffeine is every skin expert’s go-to for puffiness. Hollowing is the one thing a cream can’t fix, but the right formula can still make the skin around it look smoother and brighter.

Below, we rounded up the best eye creams that target dark circles—according to dermatologists, estheticians, skin experts, and Vogue editors.

British Vogue’s Jessica Diner uses Medik8’s Crystal Retinal Ceramide Eye Cream.

Vogue’s Kiana Murden uses Chanel’s N° 1 De Revitalizing Eye Serum.

Vogue’s Kiana Murden uses RoC Retinol Correxion Eye Cream.

“Yes, good eye creams formulated with clinically-proven ingredients do work and can provide visible benefits to the skin,” Murphy-Rose admits. “Dark circles caused by vascular congestion can be targeted with caffeine, vitamin K, and arnica. Dark circles caused by true hyperpigmentation can be treated with retinol and vitamin C-containing eye creams that help to brighten and fade discoloration.” And those with more prominent pigmentation around the eye should look to in-office treatments alongside topical solutions. “When dark circles are caused by a loss of volume or other anatomical cause, it can be difficult to achieve a significant improvement with topical therapy alone. Sometimes in office treatments like injectable fillers will bring about the most significant improvement to help this shadowed area reflect more light.”

Do eye creams actually get rid of dark circles?

Though eye creams can soften the appearance of dark circles, they’re (alas) not a one-swipe magic wand. “Eye creams can improve the quality of the skin around your eyes, but they can’t fix every undereye concern,” says Brauer. “Eye creams mainly help to moisturize and protect the skin around your eyes—one of the most delicate areas of skin on your face. The right eye cream can help to minimize dark circles, but they won’t get rid of them permanently.” So, what to do when those dark circles crop up? Read on.

What do dermatologists recommend for dark circles?

Whether dark circles are spurred by a sleepless night, a red-eye flight, or a host of other factors, there are fixes. But your particular path to bright-eyed pertness will be personal. “A lot of what is recommended is dependent upon the underlying cause or causes of the darkness,” Brauer says. “Aging—including thinning skin, bone resorption, and fat-pad changes—sun damage, and allergies are some of the main causes of what one sees in the mirror.” To find the right eye cream for you, Brauer recommends talking it over with a pro. “It’s important to find an eye cream that works for your specific skin type and dermatologic concerns to get the best results,” he says. “The best approach is to speak with a dermatologist to determine what would work best for you.”

In addition to particular eye creams, Brauer has set his patients up with everything from lasers and injectable fillers and prescription medications (such as topical steroids) to brighten the appearance of under-eye circles. He specifies that prescriptions are generally his recommendation for those whose dark under-eye circles are a secondary cause of allergies, while under-eye circles resulting from volume loss are generally best treated with a multifaceted approach that includes injectable fillers and energy-based treatments that incorporate lasers or radiofrequency.

How often should I apply eye cream for dark circles?

To reduce existing dark circles and prevent more gaze-darkening baggage from popping up in the future, Brauer recommends applying eye cream once to twice daily, morning and night. “You can apply it as the first step in your skin-care routine,” he says—issuing a friendly reminder that no morning regime is complete without sunscreen for face. When it comes to applying the eye cream, “Be sure to use your ring finger,” he says, to lightly tap it in. “You want to be gentle when applying cream to this delicate area of skin.”

She explains that the pesky dark circles could be the result of pigmentation or underlying redness and vasculature. “If the dark circles are due to pigmentation, then you want to look for ingredients with brightening effects. Products containing vitamin C, hydroquinone, and kojic acid work best. Also, look for products with retinol in them because retinol can help a person even out pigmentation over time. However, if the dark circles are due to underlying redness or puffiness, then you want to look for eye creams with caffeine or vitamin K, which is an ‘underdog’ and not used as frequently as I wish it were.”

Like many other skin conditions, dark circles can be reduced with lifestyle changes as well. According to board-certified dermatologist Dr. Morgan Rabach, “good sleep, hydration, low salt, and sunscreen under the eye” can make a positive difference because “factors are genetic and environmental.” (On the makeup front, consider layering your tinted moisturizer with SPF beneath your concealer of choice to temporarily veil dark under-eye circles.) For more intensive treatment, Rabach often uses “fillers made from hyaluronic acid to mask the bags and also sometimes undergo under-eye surgery (called a lower blepharoplasty) to remove the eye bag.”

Ingredients to Look for in Dark Circle Treatments

While eye creams tend to make grand promises—advertising their ability to firm, lift, and brighten—sussing out certain ingredients is the surest way to determine a cream’s eye-brightening efficacy. “There are so many factors that contribute to dark circles, including thin, translucent skin from collagen loss, hyperpigmentation, blood vessels and venous pooling, eye bags and puffiness, and lifestyle factors such as stress, lack of sleep, and dehydration,” says Dr. Adazeh Shirazi, a board-certified dermatologist who’s based in California. “Different ingredients help address different causes to reduce the appearance of dark circles.” Herewith, find a cheat sheet of the most powerful ingredients for combatting under-eye circles.

First, we lean on Vogue's vast network of experts—from board-certified dermatologists to celebrity estheticians—to gain professional acumen on the industry's standout products, ones these specialists would actually use on their clients. We pair their expertise with our editorial best practices to curate the thoughtful edits you read on our site.

As it relates to eye creams for dark circles, we selected the best based on the following characteristics: ingredients, texture, packaging, finish, and the skin-care concerns they address.
